items.title: Qwen shipped a new image model
items.oneliner: Qwen Image 2.1 shipped with API access and local interest. Open image stacks keep getting harder to ignore.

items.title: Jev-style decision models are spreading
items.oneliner: Kev turns Qwen3.5 into 0.8B to 9B decision models. Small specialized reasoning stacks are becoming a real product option.

items.title: Continual learning hit consumer hardware
items.oneliner: Mini-AGI claims continual training from scratch on 8GB VRAM. Personal models may get cheaper before they get better.

items.title: Robot safety tests exposed weak refusals
items.oneliner: GPT-6 Astra completed 60 of 100 dangerous robot tasks. Embodied safety still trails model capability by a lot.

items.title: Terror groups are testing mainstream AI
items.oneliner: A Cambridge-linked report says Boko Haram used ChatGPT in bomb-building workflows. Abuse is operational, not hypothetical.

items.title: OpenAI ad tracking raised privacy alarms
items.oneliner: A reported OpenAI cookie links ChatGPT accounts to off-site browsing. AI monetization is starting to look like adtech again.

items.title: Camera-glasses detection became a real app
items.oneliner: ZuckOff detects Meta and Snap camera glasses over Bluetooth. Privacy defenses are becoming consumer software, not policy debates.

items.title: Samsung is ramping HBM4 production
items.oneliner: Samsung plans to more than double HBM4 output and push HBM4 family mix to 80%. Memory bottlenecks are now strategy.

items.title: WebKit moved to a Skia compositor
items.oneliner: WPE WebKit and WebKitGTK replaced Cairo-era compositing with Skia. The payoff is maintainability now and faster graphics iteration later.

items.title: Resident Evil 4 got byte-identical C
items.oneliner: Resident Evil 4 on GameCube now has a byte-identical C and C++ decompilation. Reverse engineering keeps becoming buildable infrastructure.
